title: quercus pagoda f. intermedia
intro: Quercus pagoda f. intermedia, commonly known as the Chinese Corkbark Oak, is a deciduous tree native to China, characterized by its corky bark and broad leaves. It has been traditionally used in medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and respiratory issues, due to its potential health benefits of reducing inflammation, improving immune function, and acting as an antioxidant. The therapeutic actions of Quercus pagoda f. intermedia include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral activities, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins. The plant's bioactive constituents also exhibit antioxidant and free radical scavenging activities, which may contribute to its potential therapeutic effects.
